title: Published fund rates and returns, Kenya
why: The Capital Markets Authority licenses collective investment schemes but publishes no fund yield, so a rate can only come from the manager offering it. Every figure here was read from the manager's own page or its own factsheet, and carries the label the manager put on it, the period it covers and the date it was read. Nothing is converted between bases, nothing is annualised that the manager did not annualise, and no fund appears without a figure of its own.
gate: A fund is only carried when its scheme appears in static_data/cis_licensees_KE.json, the CMA's own register.
bases_warning: These figures are NOT like-for-like and must never be ranked against each other without their labels. A daily yield, an effective annual yield, a weekly average and a calendar-year net return are four different measurements. Some are gross of the 15 per cent withholding tax and some net of fees; each row states which, in the manager's own words.

funds.strategy: Multi-asset strategy fund with a long/short trading model, investing in global and local markets: single stocks and stock indices, fixed income, derivatives, precious metals, currencies and commodities globally; cash, fixed income, NSE derivatives, ETFs and NSE equities locally.

not_on_file.status: most licensed schemes still do not publish a current rate in a readable page
not_on_file.swept: 35 schemes on the first pass, 37 on the second with up to four candidate pages each
not_on_file.why: Two passes over the licensed schemes' own sites, rendered in a real browser, found a labelled rate on six of them. The rest publish inside a PDF factsheet, publish as an image, or do not publish a rate on the site at all. Nothing was taken without a label: Nabo Capital's 'Unlock up to 13% p.a.' is marketing copy, and a unit price such as Zimele's 'Ksh 30.7588' is a price, not a rate.
not_on_file.next: The remaining schemes need their factsheet PDFs located and read one at a time, the way the MansaX factsheet was. Rates are added as their own primary sources are found, never from an aggregator.

metrics_warning: THE FIGURES ON THIS FILE ARE NOT ONE METRIC. Each fund carries the figure its own manager published, under the manager's own name for it: a one year return, an effective annual yield, a year-to-date return, an annualised net IRR since inception, or a board whose metric the manager never states. A one year return is twelve months of performance already earned. An effective annual yield is a rate quoted per annum from a shorter period. A year-to-date return is only the months of this year so far. They are different quantities and the terminal ranks none of them against another.
live_boards_note: Several managers publish their rate as a TICKER that changes: Etica, Madison, Nabo, Kuza and Zimele. A figure read off a ticker is true of the moment it was read and of nothing else, so each of those funds carries the date it was read, and where the figure has moved since the last read the one it replaced is kept beside it. None of them is a one year return.
